thought.text: CSRF is required. Let me obtain a CSRF token from the login page and use it:

reasoning_content:
CSRF protection is enabled. I need to first obtain a CSRF token. In Zammad, the CSRF token for API sign-in is typically obtained by doing a GET request (like /api/v1/sessions or the login page) that sets a cookie, and the CSRF token is extracted from there.

Let's see how the login page works. The root / returns the login page with a csrf-token meta. Let's use that approach: GET / to obtain the token, then POST to /api/v1/signin with the token attached as the X-CSRF-Token header and with cookies included.

action.command:
docker exec zammad-devcontainer-devcontainer-1 bash -lc '
cd /tmp
rm -f cj.txt
# GET root page, capture cookies and csrf meta token
HTML=$(curl -s --max-time 60 -c cj.txt http://127.0.0.1:3000/)
CSRF=$(echo "$HTML" | grep -o "name=\"csrf-token\" content=\"[^\"]*\"" | sed "s/.*content=\"\([^\"]*\)\".*/\1/")
echo "CSRF_TOKEN_LEN=${#CSRF}"
curl -s --max-time 60 -b cj.txt -c cj.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/v1/signin \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-CSRF-Token: $CSRF" \
  -d "{\"login\":\"admin@example.com\",\"password\":\"test\"}" \
  -o /tmp/signin.json -w "LOGIN_HTTP=%{http_code}\n"
echo "--- response (first 600 chars) ---"
head -c 600 /tmp/signin.json
echo
'
